_meta.description: Vietnamese-specific adversarial panel for POST-VERIFY-PLAN.md §3. Catches: (a) tokenizer silently stripping/lowercasing diacritics → diacritic group cosine collapses ≥0.95; (b) NFC↔NFD divergence → tokenizer not normalizing internally, cosine <0.999; (c) tone-mark collapse → all six tones embedded identically, cosine >0.99; (d) cross-lingual EN↔VI semantic collapse <0.75. NFD variants computed via Python unicodedata.normalize('NFD', s) and inlined as \u-escapes so the JSON parser preserves exact byte sequence.

assertion.rationale: diacritics must matter — if tokenizer lowercases/strips, the two collapse
common sentence; diacritic-stripped form is grammatical but semantically different
place names + season; diacritic loss == different proper nouns
sữa (milk) vs sua (clean/rinse) — meaning genuinely changes
noun phrase; stripped form is informal latin transliteration
NFC vs NFD must normalize internally — bytes differ, vector must match
same phrase as vi-dia-001 — NFD form must produce same vector
NFD with multi-combining-mark syllable (Nội = N + o + dot-below + circumflex)
stress-test horn (ư = u + horn-mark U+031B) decomposition
ướng (u + horn + o + horn + acute) is the worst-case combining sequence
no-tone vs acute (sắc): ghost vs cheek/mother — distinguish but don't orthogonalize
no-tone vs grave (huyền): ghost vs but/that
acute vs hook-above (hỏi): cheek vs grave/tomb
tilde (ngã) vs dot-below (nặng): horse/code vs rice-seedling/plate
grave vs tilde: closes the 6-tone matrix in 5 pairs
canonical EN↔VI semantic equivalence; granite-r2 explicit VI training should land here
